questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Creating tasks and choosing priorities”?
options: Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
`vTaskDelayUntil` preserves the intended period, but long blocking work can still miss a deadline.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
questions.answer: Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
questions.explanation:
Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
Why: A task is a function with its own stack and execution context; `xTaskCreate` registers it with the scheduler. Set priority from a real timing need: an overactive high-priority task can starve lower-priority work. Arduino `loop()` is also an RTOS task, so plan shared access to Serial and peripherals.
